circuit_928 - two independent sub-circuits sharing one bottom ground rail. LEFT: 60V source -> 4ohm -> 20mF -> 5V source -> back along the bottom rail; GND symbol hangs off that rail at x=439. RIGHT: 4A current source in parallel with 10ohm, that node feeds a 2H inductor into a 25mF cap that returns to the same bottom rail.

NET MAP (6 nets, 9 components):
  0  = the bottom rail, y~605-622 from x=130 to x=840, plus the GND stub at (439,631). Terminals: 60V bottom (4.1), 5V bottom (6.1), 4A source bottom (5.1), 10ohm bottom (3.1), 25mF bottom (7.1), GND (8.0).
  n3 = 60V positive/top terminal -> up x=127 -> top-left rail y~405 -> left lead of the 4ohm resistor at (185,413).
  n1 = right lead of 4ohm (266,408) -> top rail -> left plate of the 20mF capacitor (324,406).
  n2 = right plate of 20mF (388,406) -> top rail -> down the x=432 column -> top (+) terminal of the 5V source.
  n4 = right-section upper-left node: top of the 4A source (578,460) -> top rail y~415 from x=581 to x=722 -> top of the 10ohm resistor (699,435) at site S13 -> left lead of the 2H inductor (722,417).
  n5 = right lead of the 2H inductor (810,414) -> right column x~840 -> top plate of the 25mF capacitor (837,472).

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all four taken as junctions):
  S13 (699,419) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the top rail runs left-to-right and the 10ohm's top lead ends on it. No hop, no pass-through geometry. 'crossing' is not even expressible for a degree-3 T; leaving it unjoined would strand the 10ohm's top lead on a one-terminal net.
  S22 (579,607) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. T where the 4A current source's bottom lead lands on the bottom rail. The alternative (rail passes under, source bottom floats) would leave the 4A source with no return path - electrically impossible for a current source.
  S23 (701,607) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. T where the 10ohm's bottom lead lands on the bottom rail. Same argument: not joining leaves the 10ohm bottom on a one-terminal net.
  S24 (439,609) deg=4 hop_score=3.6 -> JUNCTION. This is the one 4-way in the sheet: the column carrying the 5V source's negative terminal comes down from above, the bottom rail runs through horizontally (60V bottom on the left, the whole right-hand circuit on the right), and the GND symbol's stub continues below. I zoomed the pixels at (510,610) w=90 z=7: the rail is one continuous unbroken stroke from x=130 through x=580 and there is no semicircular hop or sideways jog at x=439; the reported hop_score comes from the small pen wiggle at (437,570) well above the crossing, not from the crossing itself. Reading it as a CROSSING would split the node into {5V bottom, GND} and {60V bottom, right-section bottom rail}, which breaks the left loop entirely - the 60V/4ohm/20mF/5V mesh would have no return path - and would also leave the whole right-hand circuit with no ground reference. Electrical impossibility settles it: junction.

PORT FIXES (three terminals had landed on handwritten value-label ink, each producing a one-terminal net):
  #1 Resistor (4ohm) t1: was port p2 @(266,378), which is a stroke of the '4R' label sitting just above the box. Moved to p4 @(266,408), the real right-hand lead on the y~406 rail (wire run of length 59, the same run that reaches the capacitor's left plate). Removed spurious net n4.
  #0 Capacitor (20mF) t0: was port p1 @(373,371), a stroke of the '20mF' label. Moved to p4 @(324,406), the real left plate lead. Removed spurious net n1(old).
  #2 Inductor (2H) t1: was port p3 @(800,385), a stroke of the '2H' label. Moved to p4 @(810,414), the real right-hand lead (wire run of length 84 - the same run that reaches the 25mF top plate, which is why old n6 and n7 were both singletons).
After these three fixes every net has at least two terminals and the netlist matches the drawing.

Other checks: #7 Capacitor's p2 @(890,487) is the '25mF' label and was correctly not used. #3, #4, #5, #6, #8 ports were already on the real leads. All classes match the drawn symbols (the 4A symbol is a circle with a down arrow = I-DC; both 60V and 5V circles carry +/- bars = V-DC). No 3-terminal parts on this sheet, so no pin-order questions. Non-critical sites S0/S1/S3/S4/S6/S7/S9/S10/S14/S15/S17/S19/S20 are all handwritten-label or component-symbol ink touching a wire and were left at the tracer's default; none of them changes the netlist.
